headline: High: Plandex can write and execute against shared files while Cognee handles sensitive support/finance data, creating leakage and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests documents, workflows, and support history, so if Plandex writes attacker-controlled content into a shared project directory, Cognee could treat it as trusted input. Cognee has session memory and multiple instances; Plandex reads/writes the filesystem and stages changes in a plan-local sandbox, so the bridge is plausible even without a documented shared channel.
conditions: IF Plandex can place files into a directory Cognee later ingests
IF Cognee parses file contents as instructions or workflow data without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate Cognee input directories from Plandex workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add provenance tags to all files before Cognee reads them
Review any shared folder mounts before running both agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while Plandex has broad network egress and can read/write the filesystem. If they share a workspace, Plandex can exfiltrate sensitive files through its model-provider or cloud calls. The pairwise leakage path is direct enough to warrant high severity.
conditions: IF Cognee stores sensitive support or finance data in a directory Plandex can read
IF Plandex sends file contents to its backend or model provider during planning
mitigations: Keep sensitive Cognee data outside Plandex-readable paths
Run Plandex with a non-shared workspace
Block outbound network access for Plandex during sensitive tasks
Use redacted copies of documents for any shared workflow
Audit file permissions on the shared project directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with agentic user/tenant isolation, but Plandex has per-plan shared state via a backend plus unrestricted filesystem write and git-state modification. If both operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent edits and staged changes can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The overlap is a default write-conflict risk.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace
IF Plandex auto-applies staged changes while Cognee also writes artifacts there
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Disable auto-apply in Plandex for shared repos
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file
Commit Cognee outputs only after Plandex finishes
Review git diffs before any apply step

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, and successful implementations, which Plandex could consume as planning input. Plandex is a coding tool that can execute shell commands and modify git state, so unverified Cognee output could cascade into concrete code or repo actions. The pathway exists, but Plandex's review-then-apply sandbox reduces blast radius below high.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Cognee-generated decisions or workflows as authoritative requirements
IF the operator enables auto-apply or skips review of staged changes
mitigations: Require human review of Cognee-derived plans before apply
Mark Cognee outputs as untrusted inputs in Plandex
Disable auto-apply mode
Add a verification checklist for any generated code or commands

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while Plandex can read files and send context to a model provider or cloud backend. If EU personal data or regulated support records flow into Plandex without a DPA or residency controls, the pair can create a compliance breach. Only Cognee is cited for the sensitive data class because the compliance issue is driven by its data scope plus Plandex's outbound processing.
conditions: IF regulated personal data from Cognee is processed by Plandex
IF Plandex sends that data to a third-party model provider or cloud service
mitigations: Exclude regulated records from Plandex inputs
Confirm a DPA and residency terms before sharing data
Use self-hosted model endpoints where available
Redact personal data before passing artifacts to Plandex
Document retention and deletion handling for shared files
